data.title: S&P 500 flatline masks historic churn across individual stocks - Nomura
data.description:
While the headline S&P 500 index (SPY) (VOO) appears placid on the surface, underlying individual stocks are experiencing wild volatility reminiscent of a full-blown crisis, according to Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott.

The S&P 500 moved just 0.8% over the past month, while the average constituent stock swung by 8.9%, McElligott wrote in a recent note. This 8.1 percentage point dispersion gap ranks in the 95th percentile of historical data over the past 30 years, reflecting an extraordinary level of churn beneath a deceptively quiet benchmark.

McElligott stressed that far from being complacent, the market is undergoing a substantial “rolling correction” driven by rising interest rate pressures and severe capital displacement toward artificial intelligence. Over the trailing 30 days, Technology, Media, and Telecommunication, or TMT, and Energy (XLE) were the only S&P 500 sectors to post positive returns, while rate-sensitive sectors took a heavy beating—led by real estate investment trusts (XLRE) (-9.8%), materials (XLB) (-7.9%), and financials (XLF) (-7.7%).

Damage across individual constituents is widespread: 85% of S&P 500 stocks were down more than 10% from their all-time highs, and 59% were in deep bear-market territory, down over 20%, the strategist noted. The benchmark's stability is almost single-handedly anchored by a tiny cluster of mega-cap AI leaders, with just ten stocks—led by Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), and AMD (AMD)—accounting for 70% of the market's 23% rally since late March.

data.title: Hedge funds cut Bitcoin, brokerages load up in Q2: CoinShares report
data.description:
Professional investors increased their Bitcoin (BTC-USD) holdings in second-quarter, even as overall U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings declined, according to a CoinShares report published Friday.

13F filers held 264K BTC at the end of June, up 1.3% from 261K tokens in the first-quarter. Meanwhile, total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings fell 6.3%, and non-13F holders reduced their exposure by 8.3%.

The dollar value of 13F filers’ holdings fell 13% to $15.5B as Bitcoin’s price declined 14% during the quarter. However, their share of total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF AUM rose to 22.4% from 20.8%, marking the first increase since second-quarter 2025. 

Hedge funds cut exposure as brokerages buy

Hedge funds recorded the largest reduction, cutting their Bitcoin exposure by 10.8K coins (22%) to 37.8K BTC.

DE Shaw exited its 3.7K BTC position, while Millennium Management reduced its holdings from 14.4K BTC to 7.3K BTC.

Investment advisors also trimmed exposure, reducing holdings by 4.6K BTC, or 3%, to 145.7K BTC. Brevan Howard cut its position by 9.6K BTC to 4.1K BTC.

The advisors nevertheless accounted for roughly 55% of all reported 13F Bitcoin holdings.

At the same time, brokerage holdings more than doubled to 38.5K BTC from 17K BTC. Jane Street added 10.9K BTC to reach 16.9K BTC, while Morgan Stanley (MS) held 10.4K BTC. However, Morgan Stanley’s Q1 filing was excluded from the earlier comparison, partly affecting the increase.

Bank of Montreal (BMO) and VanEck Associates each added roughly 2.6K BTC.

Other notable sellers included Avenir Tech, which reduced its position by 2.8K BTC, SIG Holding, which cut 2.4K BTC, and IMC-Chicago, which reduced its holdings by 2.3K BTC.

Government and university endowment holdings remained broadly unchanged, while private-equity exposure rose 5% to 6.9K BTC.

Now, the third-quarter filings will show whether brokerage buying continues and whether professional investors maintain their Bitcoin exposure following the second-quarter decline.

data.title: Visa set to continue gains for seven straight sessions; up nearly 2.5%
data.description:
Visa (V) is set to extend its winning streak to seven consecutive sessions as the stock jumped nearly 2.5% during afternoon trading on Friday.

The company gained nearly 4.25% over the previous six sessions. Overall, the stock has risen more than 8% so far this year, compared with a nearly 13.5% gain for the broader S&P 500 Index.

Visa is up nearly 4% over the past month. The stock closed 0.8% higher on Thursday at $375.10.

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, Visa has a Hold rating, with a score of 3.43 out of 5. The company received an A+ for profitability and a B+ for momentum, while it received an F for valuation.

However, Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha analysts are bullish, rating the stock a Strong Buy and Buy, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Cyn Research said, “I view Visa as one of the more attractive ways to benefit from AI, as it can monetize agentic commerce and internal productivity gains without having to win the much riskier parts of the AI trade.”

The analyst considered stablecoins more of an opportunity than a threat, as Visa builds infrastructure across multiple coins, chains, and tokenized payment formats.

Cyn Research added that value-added services remain a major growth driver, with third-quarter revenue up 33% YoY and several portfolios consistently growing above 20%.

“Q3’s weaker profit growth initially concerned me, but one-offs, restructuring effects, and Q4 guidance make me expect earnings growth to move back above revenue growth,” the analyst concluded.

Turning to the Wall Street analyst community, 36 out of 40 analysts rated Visa Buy or higher, while three analysts rated the stock Hold, and one recommended a Sell.

data.title: Astera Labs, Semtech downgraded by Northland Capital on risk-reward
data.description:
Astera Labs (ALAB) and Semtech (SMTC) were downgraded by Northland Capital Markets on Friday, as the investment firm cited a declining risk-reward.

“Coming into earnings, we are not confident that earnings will be strong enough to lift AI semiconductor companies,” Northland analyst Gus Richard wrote in a note to clients. “We believe connectivity companies are best positioned to outperform, but SMTC and ALAB are above our price targets, so we are downgrading. Risks continue to increase as growth is increasingly dependent on debt and AI models lose pricing power.”

Richard lowered his rating on Astera and Semtech to Market Perform.

For Astera, Richard said that a “significant portion” of the company's revenue comes from a limited number of customers. “The loss or a significant reduction in, demand from one or a few of its top end customers would adversely affect our operations and financial condition,” Richard explained.

For Semtech, the company has built its business via acquisitions and there is the concern that other objectives could be pushed aside by the push for additional acquisitions, Richard said.

“Failure to successfully identify, acquire, and integrate a company at a favorable price may adversely impact the company’s financial position and operating results,” Richard said, adding that the Sierra Wireless acquisition could wind up being a negative. “The combination of the two companies may not produce a coherent combined product offering resulting in inefficiencies and little revenue growth.”

data.title: Caledonia Mining slides after cutting guidance for full-year production, raising cost outlook
data.description:
Caledonia Mining (CMCL) fell 2.6% in Friday's trading after reporting Q3 gold production at its Blanket mine in Zimbabwe declined 11% Y/Y to 19,106 oz, citing a shortage of compressed air at certain high-grade, high-volume mining areas and the temporary retention of gold within the processing circuit.

Caledonia (CMCL) said it expects production to normalize during Q4, as two of the new compressors have now been deployed and the last two have been released from the port and are being transported to the mine.

Due to the lower-than-expected production in Q3, Caledonia (CMCL) lowered Blanket production guidance for FY 2026 to a range of 69,000-72,500 oz from its previous outlook for 72,000-76,500 oz; the revised full-year guidance implies production at Blanket of 19,800-23,300 oz.

Reflecting the lower expected production volumes, the company also raised its full-year on-mine cost guidance to $1,700-$1,900/oz sold from a prior view $1,600-$1,800/oz sold, and hiked all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,650-$2,850/oz sold from its earlier forecast of $2,500-$2,700/oz AISC.

"Although we have revised our guidance for 2026 to reflect the third-quarter performance, Blanket remains a robust and cash-generative operation," Caledonia (CMCL) CEO Mark Learmonth said.

data.title: Cable One plunges on report lender filed lawsuit to block Mega Broadband deal
data.description:
Cable One (CABO) cratered 35% after a report that a lender filed a lawsuit seeking to block the cable operator from purchasing a 55% equity stake in Mega Broadband from financial sponsor GTCR.

CoBank, which says it holds about $1.1 billion in secured credit issued by Cable One (CABO), asked a federal judge in New York to issue an emergency restraining order to prevent the company from transferring about $480 million for the Mega Broadband purchase, according a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited the lawsuit. 

Cable One (CABO) faces a Friday deadline to complete the purchase.

The lender said the transfer of funds would make Cable One “sink deeper into insolvency and make its remaining assets unreasonably small given its already large debts.”  

Representatives for Cable One, CoBank and GTCR didn’t immediately respond to Bloomberg requests for comment.

data.title: Jefferies fined $650K over deficient electronic blue sheets reporting
data.description:
Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) was fined $650K by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission over deficient electronic blue sheets reporting.

EBS data files contain both trading and account holder information, and are said to provide regulators with the ability to analyze a firm's trading activity.

The proceedings rose out of Jefferies' failure to submit to the regulator complete and accurate data in response to its requests from at least July 2018 through July 2024, resulting in incomplete or deficient reporting.

The SEC routinely sends requests for securities trading records to market makers, broker-dealers, and/or clearing firms.

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Delta slides on earnings miss, Tesla gains on China sales & more
data.description:
Wall Street regained some momentum on Friday, after the AI trade came under pressure on Thursday.

S&P 500 (SP500) +0.4%, the Dow (DJI) +0.6%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.5%.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

Delta Air Lines drops 5% on Q3 earnings miss and lowered profit guidance: Delta Air Lines  (DAL) shares fell about 5% in premarket trading after the carrier reported September-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.72 per share, missing the $1.82 consensus estimate. Adjusted revenue rose 16% to $17.59 billion but came in slightly below expectations. The airline lowered its full-year profit outlook to about $5.35 per share, citing elevated fuel costs that surged 62% to $4.14 billion in the quarter. Delta absorbed more than $500 million in additional fuel costs compared with its early July guidance and expects to absorb $6 billion in higher fuel expenses for the full year. 

Apple slips on order cuts as SpaceX spectrum deal hits telecom stocks: Apple (AAPL) shares  fell about 2.6% in premarket trading after reports that the company cut component orders for some iPhone 18 Pro models following weaker-than-expected demand. Separately, telecom stocks dropped sharply after SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license that could pave the way for increased competition with established wireless carriers. AT&T fell 8%, Verizon Communications declined 7.8%, and T-Mobile US dropped 7.6%, while SpaceX shares rose 4.3%. The acquisition would give Elon Musk's space and satellite company access to spectrum needed to expand its mobile ambitions.

Tesla advances 3.6% as Shanghai EV deliveries rise 5% in September: Tesla (TSLA) shares  gained about 3.6% after data from the China Passenger Car Association showed deliveries of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles from Tesla's Shanghai factory rose 5% year-over-year to 95,366 units in September. The results extended the automaker's streak of annual sales gains to 11 consecutive months. Shipments of Shanghai-built vehicles grew 13.7% in the third quarter, even as global deliveries declined 2.1% from a year earlier. Tesla is offering discounts in China on selected Model Y and Model 3 variants through the end of October as competition in the world's largest auto market remains intense.

Ambarella jumps 5.3% on reports of Qualcomm takeover interest: Ambarella (AMBA) shares  rose 5.3% following reports that Qualcomm may be working with advisers on a possible deal to acquire the chip designer. The speculation, circulated via a Betaville alert, follows prior reports that Ambarella is in talks with potential buyers including NXP Semiconductors. Discussions are said to be at an advanced stage, though there is no certainty any deal will materialize. Betaville first reported takeover speculation surrounding Ambarella in late July, when the stock jumped 16% on reports of NXP's interest.
